=== SELLER DOCUMENTS (untrusted) ===
From: Harbourglass Ventures Pty Ltd (Seller) counsel
To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2. As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security is included.

4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.

5. Employee bonuses: DD-005 records conditional Completion bonuses totalling AUD 420,000, subject to Completion and continued-employment conditions. Those amounts do NOT appear in the draft Completion funds flow. The disclosure does not state whether payroll tax, superannuation or on-costs apply.

6. Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). As at 22 September 2026 the material does not establish whether an unauthorised person accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. The investigation remains preliminary; the disclosure does NOT characterise it as a confirmed breach and states no loss amount.

7. Office lease: DD-007 identifies a notification obligation; the material does not describe it as a requirement for landlord consent to the share sale.

8. Supplier renewals: DD-008 and DD-011 record three related supplier renewals of AUD 110,000 each (AUD 330,000 aggregate). Read together for timing/scope. The disclosure does not state whether each is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or in the ordinary course.

9. Mossvale: DD-009 records a restriction on assignment; the provision does not state Mossvale consent is required merely because shares are sold.

10. Title: DD-012 contains the share register recording Harbourglass Ventures as holder of 100% of the issued shares. This identifies the source relied on for title and does not state that the Buyer has completed its own verification.

11. Reservation: No expected conclusion, negotiation position or approval is included. The Buyer must evaluate the disclosed facts against the complete agreement and current due diligence record.
=== END SELLER DOCUMENTS ===

Review the Seller's documents against the buyer's interests. For EACH of these issues, state the Seller's position, what the buyer should want, and your recommendation with a one-line reason:

# Project Kestrel: Buyer Issues Review (SPA-N-001 to SPA-N-016)

**Scope:** Review of Harbourglass's Seller Update and Disclosure Letter (SPA-003) from the Buyer's side. Figures are AUD. Points on NSW limitation periods, privacy notification and payroll tax are flagged for confirmation by NSW and Australian specialist counsel.

**Headline concern:** The Seller's package would push most of the economic risk to Wattlebridge. Its general disclosure, buyer-knowledge bar, universal caps and post-completion Riverlark release would leave the Buyer holding the known issues.

---

### SPA-N-001: General liability cap
- **Seller position:** General Warranty Claims capped at 20% of price (AUD 4,800,000).
- **Buyer should want:** A general cap materially higher, with fundamental and tax claims outside it (see N-004 and N-016). Opening position: 50% (AUD 12,000,000), fallback about 30% (AUD 7,200,000).
- **Recommendation:** **Counter.** A 20% cap is low for a AUD 24m deal with known open issues worth several million dollars.

### SPA-N-002: De minimis and basket
- **Seller position:** AUD 25,000 de minimis per claim. AUD 250,000 deductible basket, recoverable only as excess above basket (about 1.04% of price).
- **Buyer should want:** De minimis of about AUD 10,000. Tipping basket of about AUD 120,000 (0.5% of price), so that once exceeded, the full amount is recoverable. Claims above de minimis should count toward the basket. The Seller's wording is unclear on whether sub-threshold claims count, and this must be fixed.
- **Recommendation:** **Counter.** A deductible basket of this size removes the first AUD 250k of any warranty loss and the wording is ambiguous.

### SPA-N-003: General claims time limit
- **Seller position:** 18 months from Completion for general claims, and any Claim limitation applies to all Claims.
- **Buyer should want:** General warranties at 36 months (minimum 24), which covers at least one full audit and tax cycle. Tax claims should run to 60 days after the statute of limitations. Fundamental claims should run for 6 years, subject to confirming the NSW position for contract claims.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject.** 18 months is too short to surface reporting, tax and contract issues in this business.

### SPA-N-004: Fundamental/Title regime
- **Seller position:** Capacity and title warranties subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties.
- **Buyer should want:** Fundamental warranties (title, capacity, authority, share capital) capped at the full purchase price, with a longer time limit as in N-003. They should sit outside the general cap and basket.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject.** Title is what Wattlebridge is buying, so it cannot be capped at a fraction of price.

### SPA-N-005: Fraud carve-out
- **Seller position:** The Seller's documents do not state a fraud carve-out. Clauses 9.3, 12.8 and 20.5 apply limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance to "all Claims of any nature," which would arguably capture fraud.
- **Buyer should want:** An express carve-out so that fraud, dishonesty and wilful concealment sit outside caps, time limits, exclusive remedy, non-reliance and the knowledge bar. Specialist counsel should confirm the position on non-reliance clauses against misleading or deceptive conduct claims.
- **Recommendation:** **Insert.** The absence of a carve-out, combined with "all Claims of any nature," is a gap that needs closing.

### SPA-N-006: Disclosure scope
- **Seller position:** General disclosure of the whole data room (DD-002 to DD-012), the Accounts, statutory registers and public records (Disclosure Letter 1.1 and 1.2).
- **Buyer should want:** Disclosure only where specific, fairly disclosed in reasonable detail against a specific warranty. No general data-room or public-register disclosure, and no disclosure of documents by reference alone.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject.** General disclosure of the entire data room would effectively neutralise every warranty.

### SPA-N-007: Buyer knowledge qualifier
- **Seller position:** Buyer has no claim for anything the Buyer or its advisers knew, including anything discoverable from the data room or public records (Clause 8.3).
- **Buyer should want:** Deletion, plus an express pro-sandbagging clause confirming the Buyer's rights are unaffected by its knowledge. Australian authority on this point is not settled, so express wording is needed.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject.** Combined with N-006, the Buyer would lose claims on every issue it has identified in diligence.

### SPA-N-008: Bluefen consent
- **Seller position:** Consent "addressed"; Seller uses reasonable endeavours and treats consent as satisfied on delivery of written consent. Disclosure Letter 2 says no final written consent is included and conditions in clause 11.3 are not shown as satisfied. Bluefen is about AUD 3.6m (~30%) of FY26 revenue.
- **Buyer should want:** Unconditional written Bluefen consent, with all clause 11.3 conditions satisfied, as a condition precedent to Completion. Wattlebridge should have a walk right if it is not delivered. "Reasonable endeavours" is not acceptable. The Seller's summary ("addressed") conflicts with its own disclosure and should be corrected.
- **Recommendation:** **Make a condition precedent.** Roughly 30% of revenue is at stake and the Seller's own disclosure confirms consent is outstanding.

### SPA-N-009: Riverlark facility
- **Seller position:** About AUD 3.2m outstanding, to be addressed by a release after Completion. Disclosure Letter 3 says the facility is not repaid and no discharge is included.
- **Buyer should want:** Payoff letter and security discharge delivered at Completion. The payoff amount deducted from price in the funds flow, consistent with the debt-free/cash-free basis. Discharge of any registered security (including PPSR release) and no Buyer-funded debt.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject post-Completion release.** Under a debt-free/cash-free price, the Seller must repay this debt from proceeds at Completion.

### SPA-N-010: Employee bonuses
- **Seller position:** AUD 420,000 conditional Completion bonuses are "a matter for the Seller" and not itemised in the funds flow. Disclosure Letter 5 says payroll tax and super treatment are unstated.
- **Buyer should want:** Bonuses, employer on-costs (payroll tax at the NSW rate, and superannuation guarantee on bonuses at the current rate, to be confirmed) treated as debt-like items reducing price or paid by the Seller. Specific indemnity for all related liabilities.
- **Recommendation:** **Counter and deduct.** The bonuses are a pre-Completion liability that the Seller has not priced.

### SPA-N-011: Ironquay IP indemnity
- **Seller position:** Indemnity limited to the SOW3 payment and "considered adequate." Disclosure Letter 4 says AUD 180,000 is open, no payment receipt or confirmatory assignment is in the data room, and transfer of SOW3 Project Materials depends on clearing every SOW3 fee.
- **Buyer should want:** Payment of all open Ironquay amounts before Completion, or deduction from price. A confirmatory IP assignment delivered at Completion. A specific indemnity covering all Ironquay claims and IP title defects, outside the general cap.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject.** The Buyer may not own the SOW3 IP until the AUD 180k is paid, and the indemnity is narrower than the exposure.

### SPA-N-012: Export/privacy incident
- **Seller position:** Described as "preliminary" and "not expected to be material" (Schedule 6). Disclosure Letter 6 says the file may contain about 1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, timestamps), whether access occurred is unknown, and notification is unconfirmed.
- **Buyer should want:** Completed forensic review before Completion. Confirmed assessment under the Privacy Act 1988 (Cth) notifiable data breaches scheme, which generally requires assessment within 30 days of suspicion (specialist confirmation needed). Specific indemnity for notification, regulatory and remediation costs, outside the cap and basket. Retention or escrow pending outcome. A warranty that there are no other incidents.
- **Recommendation:** **Specific indemnity plus retention.** The Seller's "not material" label is not supported by its own disclosure.

### SPA-N-013: Sandbar renewals
- **Seller position:** Three renewals of AUD 110,000 each (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs. Disclosure Letter 8 says it is not stated whether they are unavoidable, terminable, accrued or ordinary course.
- **Buyer should want:** Confirmation of contract terms, termination rights and timing. Any pre-Completion committed amounts treated as debt-like or working capital adjustments. The three renewals read together should be assessed as one commitment.
- **Recommendation:** **Verify and adjust if pre-Completion.** Ordinary-course status is asserted, not shown.

### SPA-N-014: Category separation
- **Seller position:** No separation. Fundamental, tax and IP warranties all sit under the general regime (Seller Update, Tax/IP and Fundamental entries).
- **Buyer should want:** Separate regimes: general warranties; fundamental/title warranties (N-004); tax indemnity and tax warranties (N-016); and specific indemnities for known issues (N-008 to N-012).
- **Recommendation:** **Reject a single regime.** Combining them gives the Seller the caps and short time limits for every risk type.

### SPA-N-015: Title verification
- **Seller position:** Title evidenced by the share register (DD-012). The Seller says nothing about the Buyer's own verification.
- **Buyer should want:** Independent verification: ASIC company extract, certified share register, confirmation no options or other rights over shares, PPSR search for encumbrances, and a warranty that shares are fully paid and free from encumbrances. Fundamental warranty (N-004) covering all of this.
- **Recommendation:** **Verify independently.** The Seller's register is the Seller's own document and is not proof of title on its own.

### SPA-N-016: Tax/IP open terms
- **Seller position:** Tax and IP warranties treated as "settled" under the general regime.
- **Buyer should want:** Pre-Completion tax indemnity outside the general cap and basket, with time limits matching the tax assessment period. Full tax warranties. IP ownership and non-infringement warranties, including coverage of the Ironquay and export issues. Tax and IP covenants on pre-Completion periods.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject "settled."** Tax and IP are open items in the Seller's own disclosure and need their own regime.

---

### Cross-cutting actions
1. **Funds flow:** Riverlark payoff and bonus deduction must appear in the completion funds flow. The Seller's statement that the flow "reflects the agreed price mechanics" is inconsistent with the disclosed debt and bonuses.
2. **Conditions:** Bluefen consent and Ironquay payment should be conditions precedent to Completion, with a walk right.
3. **Specialist confirmation needed:** NSW limitation periods for contract claims, the Privacy Act notification timing, NSW payroll tax rates and superannuation treatment, and enforceability of non-reliance and pro-sandbagging wording.
